# SECURITY: verify.py renders an unvalidated ?redirect= into an <a href> on the email confirm pages — the server-side sibling of #1068

- **Kind**: bug (security) — **Priority**: should — **Project**: django-mojo
- **Board**: https://maestromojo.com/workspaces/#/board/11?item=1091
- **Source**: found while scoping #1068; same bug class, different (server-side) surface.

## Description

`mojo/apps/account/rest/verify.py` (`_render_verify`) reads the destination straight off the query string with no validation and puts it on the template context. `email_verify_confirm.html` and `email_change_confirm.html` then render it into an anchor. A `javascript:` value therefore becomes a one-click script-execution sink on the auth origin — the same shape #943 fixed for `?back=` and #1068 fixed for `?redirect=` on the hosted auth pages.

## Two notes for whoever picks this up

1. **This cannot share #1068's fix.** That one is a template-JS helper (`safeNavUrl`) inside `auth_base.html`; this is a server-side Python path. The guard has to be applied before the value reaches the context.
2. **It also violates a repo convention**: `request.GET.get(...)` instead of `request.DATA`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `?redirect=` whose scheme is not `http`/`https` never reaches the rendered `href` — the link is omitted or falls back to a safe default, matching how #943 handled a refused `?back=`
- [ ] Same-origin relative paths and legitimate cross-origin `http(s)` URLs are unchanged — the **host is deliberately not allowlisted**, consistent with #943/#1068
- [ ] Both templates and both sinks are covered, and the meta-refresh line is either guarded too or explicitly documented as non-exploitable
- [ ] Input read via `request.DATA`
- [ ] Regression test that fails on the current code
- [ ] Check `mojo/helpers/` for an existing URL-scheme helper before writing a new one

## Out of scope

- Allowlisting the redirect host
- The hosted auth pages (`#1068`, done)
- CSP (`#945`)

---

## Plan

**Build order: THIRD in this batch** (after #1089 and #1088, both landed). No file overlap with them; only `CHANGELOG.md` is shared — append to `## Unreleased`, do not disturb their entries.

### Objective

Stop an attacker-supplied `?redirect=` from reaching an `href` on the two server-rendered account confirm pages, by guarding the value **once, at the point where it enters the template context**. A refused value is dropped, so the link is omitted rather than rendered dead. Scheme only — the host stays unrestricted.

### Premise correction (verified — changes the shape of the work)

**The bug has TWO independent server-side entry points, not one.** The workspec says the guard belongs in `verify.py` and treats both templates as its consumers. That is false: `email_change_confirm.html` is rendered by a separate helper, `_render_confirm` in `mojo/apps/account/rest/user.py`, driven by `on_email_change_confirm_get`. Fixing `verify.py` alone leaves `GET /api/auth/email/change/confirm?redirect=javascript:…` fully exploitable while appearing to satisfy the "both templates covered" criterion. **Both call sites must be fixed.**

Also confirmed: the `request.GET` convention violation is `verify.py`-only — `_render_confirm` already reads `request.DATA` first (with a dead `or request.GET` fallback, see A1).

### Steps

1. **Add the shared scheme guard** — create `mojo/helpers/urls.py` with one public function, no type hints, no settings reads, no I/O, no logging:
   - `safe_nav_url(value, default="")` — returns `value` **unchanged** when it is a non-empty `str` resolving to an `http`/`https` scheme **or** carrying no scheme at all (relative reference); otherwise returns `default`. Non-`str` input returns `default`.
   - Implementation: strip `\t\r\n` anywhere and `lstrip` C0-control-and-space *before* `urlsplit`, wrap `urlsplit` in `try/except ValueError` (it raises on a malformed IPv6 authority), compare `scheme.lower()` against a module-level `SAFE_URL_SCHEMES = ("http", "https")`.
   - **Docstring must record three things**: (a) this is the server-side half of the contract whose browser-side half is `safeNavUrl()` in `auth_base.html`; (b) the **host is deliberately not restricted** — host restriction is the separate opt-in `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URLS` / `AUTH_HANDOFF_ALLOWED_URLS`; (c) why `//` and `\` are admitted here even though the sibling guard `_safe_home_url` in `mojo/apps/shortlink/rest/redirect.py` refuses protocol-relative — see A2.
2. **Guard the email-verify confirm page** — `mojo/apps/account/rest/verify.py`: import the helper; replace the `request.GET.get("redirect", "")` read with `safe_nav_url(request.DATA.get("redirect"))`; update the `_render_verify` docstring with the scheme contract.
3. **Guard the email-change confirm page** — `mojo/apps/account/rest/user.py` `_render_confirm`: see **A1**, the assignment must become exactly `redirect_url = urls.safe_nav_url(request.DATA.get("redirect"))` with the `or` clause **deleted**. **Ordering is load-bearing**: this assignment must stay above the `HttpResponseRedirect(redirect_url)` branch so that branch can never see a raw value.
4. **Tests** — see below.
5. **Docs + CHANGELOG.**

### Design decisions

- **Guard at the context boundary (Python), not in the template.** Both templates are *documented as deployment-overridable*, so a template-level filter protects only the shipped templates and a downstream override silently re-opens the hole. Sanitizing before the value enters the context protects every override and covers all three sinks per template (meta refresh, Continue anchor, Go-back anchor) with one check that cannot drift into three.
- **This satisfies the meta-refresh criterion by construction.** `redirect_url` can now only be an `http(s)`/relative value or empty, so the meta refresh is guarded whether or not a browser would have refused it — no reliance on the "browsers ignore non-web schemes in meta refresh" claim, which the plan therefore stops asserting as fact.
- **New helper in `mojo/helpers/urls.py`, not in `redirect_allowlist.py`.** Verified there is **no existing URL-scheme helper anywhere in `mojo/helpers/`**, and nothing in-tree uses Django's `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme` (unusable here: it requires a host allowlist and would reject the cross-origin destinations the criteria require to keep working). `redirect_allowlist._split` is private, absolute-URL-only (rejects `/dashboard`) and applies hostname-charset rules — reusing it would violate the "relative paths unchanged" criterion. Keeping the guard out of that file also avoids a collision with #1088/#1089, which edited it.
- **Return the value unchanged rather than a normalized absolute URL.** The browser twin returns `resolved.href`; server-side that would rewrite `/dashboard` into `https://host/dashboard`, breaking the "relative paths unchanged" criterion. Normalization is used only *inside* the judgment, never on the way out.
- **Non-`str` input is refused, not coerced.** A real consequence of the `request.DATA` conversion: `?redirect=a&redirect=b` yields a **list** and `?redirect.x=1` yields a **dict**, where `request.GET.get()` always returned a string. Fail-closed is correct and matches the repo default.
- **`HttpResponseRedirect` branch left in place.** Verified currently unreachable (`redirect_delay` is `3` whenever `success` is truthy, and the branch requires success *and* a falsy delay); Django also refuses non-`http/https/ftp` there. Deleting it is a separate cleanup — guarding the value above it is what matters.
- **Refusal shape = #943's.** Empty value → the `{% if redirect_url %}` wrapper is false → the anchor is never emitted; the template's existing "You can close this tab" fallback takes over. Note explicitly: this **omits** the element rather than hiding it, which is the first half of the acceptance clause ("omitted or falls back to a safe default").

### Amendments from the challenge round (BINDING)

**A1 — the `or request.GET.get(...)` fallback must be DELETED, not wrapped (highest-value edit).**
`_render_confirm` currently reads `request.DATA.get("redirect") or request.GET.get("redirect", "")`. An implementer preserving existing behavior would write `safe_nav_url(request.DATA.get("redirect")) or request.GET.get("redirect", "")` — and for `?redirect=javascript:alert(1)` the helper returns `""` (falsy), the `or` falls through to the **raw query value**, and the payload lands in the href. The guard is inverted into a pass-through by exactly the value it exists to stop. The fallback is dead today (for a GET, `request.DATA` mirrors `request.GET`); the fix is what would make it live. → State the post-state literally; deleting the `or` clause is mandatory, not optional.

**A2 — record why this guard is looser than its in-tree sibling.**
`mojo/apps/shortlink/rest/redirect.py::_safe_home_url` is the same check for the same reason ("anything else is dropped and the button is omitted") but **explicitly refuses protocol-relative** `//evil.test`. Ours admits it. The divergence is correct here — the acceptance criteria explicitly permit cross-origin `https://evil.com`, so refusing the equivalent `//evil.com` would be incoherent, and it matches #1068's `safeNavUrl`, which resolves via `new URL(raw, location.href)` and judges the resolved protocol. But it must be **written down** in the helper docstring, along with the note that `_safe_home_url` is deliberately **not** migrated (its input is an admin-writable setting where off-site is genuinely unwanted). Otherwise a later "unify these three guards" refactor silently loosens shortlink.

**A3 — drop the refusal logging.** The verify confirm GET carries `@md.public_endpoint()` with **no rate limit** (unlike the email-change endpoint), and `logit.warning` is a synchronous file write, so a per-refusal log line is attacker-pumpable. `repr[:200]` bounds record *size*, not record *count*. #1068's shipped shape is silent. The scoping plan offered this as its own fallback; taking it.

**A4 — drop the `verify.py` token read change.** Moving the `token` read to `request.DATA` is scope creep in a security patch: it silently admits `?token[]=x` as a new spelling and drops repeated-param last-wins semantics, and the workspec's `request.DATA` requirement is about the *redirect* read. Verified harmless either way, but out of scope.

**A5 — keep the C0 strip, but comment it and don't over-claim the tests.** Probed on the local interpreter (3.12.10): `urlsplit` already handles the C0/tab/leading-space `javascript:` variants, so the manual strip matters only on 3.10.0–3.10.11 (before the CVE-2023-24329 backport). `pyproject.toml` allows `>=3.10`, so keep it — but comment it with the CVE/version rationale in-code, and label those test cases as browser-parity documentation rather than as guards on the strip.

**A6 — collapse to a single public function.** `is_safe_nav_url` would be dead public API if only `safe_nav_url` is called. One public function; test it directly.

**A7 — contract wording.** "Same-origin relative paths" is false: `//evil.com/x`, `/\evil.com/x` and `\\evil.com/x` all parse scheme-less and navigate off-origin. Docs and CHANGELOG must say "scheme-relative and path-relative values pass through unchanged and may still resolve off-origin."

**Rebutted:** helper placement (`mojo/helpers/urls.py` sits alongside `mojo/urls.py`, but `mojo/helpers/__init__.py` is empty and nothing star-imports it — no real collision, and `request.py` hosts request-shaped helpers, which a URL scheme guard is not).

### Edge cases

- `?redirect=` absent or empty → `""` → page renders exactly as today.
- Repeated (`?redirect=a&redirect=b`) or dotted (`?redirect.x=1`) → list/dict → refused. New behavior vs `request.GET.get()` (last-wins string); worth one CHANGELOG line.
- `javascript:`, `JaVaScRiPt:`, `java<TAB>script:`, leading-space/C0 `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, `myapp://home` → all refused. Custom app schemes refused too — same consequence #1068 documented; call it out.
- `//evil.com/x` → allowed (A2).
- `http://[::1/x` → `urlsplit` raises `ValueError` → refused.
- `javascript%3Aalert(1)` → browser treats as a relative path; allowing it is correct, not a bypass.
- A value passing but embedding a stripped character → returned unchanged; Django autoescaping (neither template uses `|safe`) keeps `"` out of the attribute, so no attribute breakout.
- Error path plus refused redirect → error card with no button at all. Intended.

### Testing plan

Every live-page test asserts a **positive page marker before the negative assertion**, so it cannot pass vacuously on a 404/500.

`tests/test_helpers/safe_nav_url.py` (new, no setup):
- `test_refuses_script_and_non_web_schemes` — table over `javascript:`, case/tab/C0-padded variants, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, `myapp://home`.
- `test_allows_http_https_and_relative` — `https://…`, `http://localhost:3000/cb`, `/dashboard`, `/a?b=c#d`, `//example.com/x`. Proves the guard is not a blanket break and the host is not restricted.
- `test_refuses_non_string_and_unparsable` — `None`, `""`, `[]`, `["/a","/b"]`, `{"x":"1"}`, `123`, `http://[::1/x`.
- `test_safe_nav_url_returns_value_or_default` — safe values come back byte-identical (no normalization); refused values return `""` or a caller-supplied default.

`tests/test_verification/confirm_redirect_guard.py` (new; own setup that clears rate limits and deletes-then-creates its user — never reuse `verification.py`'s fixture):
- `test_verify_confirm_error_page_omits_javascript_redirect` — GET with a garbage token and `redirect=javascript:alert(1)`; assert 200 + "Link invalid" present, then no `javascript:` in the body. **Fails on current code** (today the Go-back anchor renders it).
- `test_verify_confirm_success_page_omits_javascript_redirect` — mint a real token in-process; assert "Email verified" present, no `javascript:` anywhere (covers the Continue anchor **and** the meta refresh), and the "close this tab" fallback rendered — proving the link was omitted, not left dead.
- `test_verify_confirm_keeps_https_redirect` / `test_verify_confirm_keeps_relative_redirect` — exact `href` preserved byte-identically (no normalization to absolute).

`tests/test_email/email_change.py` (appended section; reuses the module's setup and its email/username restore idiom; `clear_rate_limits(ip=…)` first because the endpoint carries a strict IP rate limit):
- `test_change_confirm_get_error_page_omits_javascript_redirect` — **fails on current code**.
- `test_change_confirm_get_success_page_omits_javascript_redirect`
- `test_change_confirm_get_keeps_https_redirect`

### Schema impact

None.

### Contract changes

- `GET /api/auth/verify/email/confirm` and `GET /api/auth/email/change/confirm`: a `?redirect=` whose scheme is neither `http` nor `https` (and is not scheme-less) is dropped — no button rendered, no meta refresh emitted. Status codes, page copy and every other context variable unchanged. `http(s)` and relative values render byte-identically.
- Deployments using a custom app scheme in `?redirect=` on these two links lose the button and must switch to an https universal/app link — same consequence #1068 shipped.
- A repeated `?redirect=a&redirect=b` is now refused rather than last-wins.
- Template-context guarantee for downstream overrides: `redirect_url` is always `""` or a vetted `http(s)`/relative value.
- No JSON API, endpoint signature, permission or serialization changes.
